title: Local review catches invalid write-only schema relationships

provenance.originSummary: Derived from the upstream-accepted write-only attribute schema pattern.
provenance.whyItMattered: Write-only schema can become impossible to configure when the write-only field conflicts with its required version trigger, while allowing trigger version zero prevents reliable update tracking.
provenance.genericCondition: A changed Plugin SDK resource adds a write-only counterpart and version trigger but targets the wrong ConflictsWith field and omits positive trigger validation.

description: A synthetic local-review scenario where a changed Go resource uses the formerly incorrect write-only schema shape. The correct review must apply IMPL-SCHEMA-017, flag the wrong conflict target and missing positive version validation, and leave the already symmetric RequiredWith relationship alone.

scope.notes: The fixture isolates write-only schema review; CRUD handling, lifecycle tests, and documentation are explicitly established as correct context.

mustCatch.description: The write-only field incorrectly conflicts with its required version trigger instead of the original sensitive field, making valid write-only configuration impossible and allowing both value sources together.
The write-only version trigger must use validation.IntAtLeast(1) so a configured zero cannot undermine Plugin SDK v2 change tracking.

mustNotFlag.description: Do not report the RequiredWith relationship as missing or incorrect because the write-only field and version trigger already require each other symmetrically.
Do not invent CRUD, state, test, or documentation issues when the fixture explicitly establishes those companion paths as correct and unchanged.

notes: Pair this case with the example result and review output to benchmark the upstream-backed write-only schema rule through the generic local-review workflow.
